newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai white sugar premiums up sharply as sales jump.
newsitem.headline: Thai white sugar premiums up sharply as sales jump.

text.p: Thai white sugar premiums have risen sharply on active offtake, especially from Indonesia, but raw premiums remain flat, awaiting news from China, trade sources said on Wednesday.
The March/May white premium was quoted around $13-14 over London number 5 for 100 ICUMSA from around $8 earlier this month. Current offers are between $301-$312 a tonne FOB Bangkok.
"This month alone will see more than 100,000 tonnes of white shipment to Indonesia," one trader said.
According to shipping sources, 195,700 tonnes of Thai sugar, mostly white, were or will be shipped to Indonesia between January and early February.

However, some Thai traders gave a lukewarm response to comments from the head of Indonesian state logistics agency BULOG, Beddu Amang, who said on January 16 that Indonesia will import about 500,000 tonnes of sugar in 1997.
"They bought more in 1996...perhaps over 600,000 tonnes. The market is just desperate for leads," said one trader.
Thai raw premiums for March/May slid to 0.30/0.40 U.S. cents over New York from 0.35/0.40 cents last week.
